tweet_summary: Rock-history account posts a Beatles photo captioned as 'the cover of their final album Get Back', accompanied by an AI-upscaled/restored version of the 1969 EMI House balcony photo.
why_note_decision: The 'Get Back' framing is technically off (the project was shelved and released as Let It Be; the photo ended up on the 1973 1967-1970 Blue Album), but this is well-known Beatles trivia and the original note also fails to address the more visually relevant point readers actually raise — that the image is AI-upscaled. The factual error is a small history nitpick on a non-news pop-culture tweet; rated NoteNotNeeded by raters. Not the kind of misinformation that needs correction.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. Any note here is a false positive — the 'Get Back' wording is a minor pop-history slip on a fluff tweet; readers can self-correct via top reply. A note that focuses on whether the image is AI-upscaled (without solid evidence) would also be wrong.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The photo was taken for the planned "Get Back" album, which was shelved and released as "Let It Be" with a different cover. No Beatles album titled "Get Back" was ever released, and this image was used for the 1973 compilation "1967-1970".
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Pedantic correction of a fluff music-history tweet; community rated NoteNotNeeded. The underlying historical claim is roughly accurate, but the tweet does not assert false news a reader needs help correcting.

fact_check.claim_verdict: minor misstatement of album history; no harmful misinformation
fact_check.notes: Photo was taken May 13 1969 at EMI House for the abandoned 'Get Back' project; used on the 1973 Blue Album. Tweet's framing is slightly wrong but not misleading on any matter of public consequence.

importance.lens_rationale: 118k impressions on a music-history fluff tweet; near-zero stakes for any EA/progress/safety lens.
